audience.title: Who I work with
audience.subtitle: Three different situations, one question: where is the traffic leaking.

startups.title: Startups and founders
startups.desc: You're launching, and version one has to be right: routes, rendering, schema, and analytics from day one. Fixing that later costs triple and costs you rankings.

agencies.title: Agencies and studios
agencies.desc: You have the strategy; you're missing the person who ships it in the code. I work inside your repo, under your brand, with PRs your team reviews before merge.

established.title: Established companies
established.desc: You have traffic and something is holding it back: a migration that never closed properly, dropped indexation, a CMS fighting you. We diagnose with data before touching a line.

services.title: Four ways to work together
services.subtitle: All of them start with an audit and end with something you can verify in Search Console.
services.processSubtitle: Four phases, scope agreed in writing. No mid-project surprises.
services.step1Desc: I crawl the site, read the server logs, and go through your Search Console. You get a list prioritized by real impact, not an eighty-page PDF nobody opens.
services.step2Desc: We decide what gets fixed first and what isn't worth touching. Every item carries an estimate, a risk, and the metric that will tell us whether it worked.
services.step3Desc: I work in branches, with reviewable PRs and a staging environment. Nothing reaches production before you've seen it.
services.step4Desc: I compare before and after: indexed pages, field Core Web Vitals, and queries that gained position. If something didn't move, I tell you.

servicesHub.title: Services
servicesHub.subtitle: Technical SEO, Next.js development, AI automation, and business dashboards.
servicesHub.lead: Four services held to the same standard: if it can't be measured, it doesn't get billed as a result. We start where the real bottleneck is, not where the easy sale is.
servicesHub.chooseHelp: If you're not sure which one you need, describe the problem and I'll tell you. That conversation is free.

seoTecnico.title: Technical SEO Consultant in Mexico
seoTecnico.subtitle: Audits, structured data, Core Web Vitals, and migrations. I work on the code, not on a generic checklist.
seoTecnico.ctaNote: I reply within 24-48 business hours, Mexico City time.

desarrolloWeb.title: Web Development with Next.js and Firebase
desarrolloWeb.subtitle: Apps that render on the server, load fast on 4G, and get indexed the same day they ship.
desarrolloWeb.ctaNote: You get scope, timeline, and price in writing before I write a line of code.

automatizacionIA.title: AI Automation and Chatbots
automatizacionIA.subtitle: Chatbots with real context and workflows that remove manual work. With spend limits, conversation logs, and a human who can step in.
automatizacionIA.ctaNote: If the process shouldn't be automated, I'll say so on the first call.

dashboards.title: Dashboards and Business Analytics
dashboards.subtitle: A dashboard leadership opens on Monday and understands without a walkthrough. Wired to your data, not to last week's export.
dashboards.ctaNote: We start by naming the five metrics decisions actually get made on.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: Computer science engineer. Technical SEO consultant. PMP certified.
about.lead: I studied Computer Science Engineering at Tecnológico de Monterrey, with a specialization in advanced AI for data science. Four years on, I do an uncommon mix: I write the code, and I'm also accountable for the organic traffic that code produces.
about.philosophy: How I think about the work
about.philosophyDesc: A pretty site nobody finds is an expensive brochure. A fast site with incoherent architecture isn't much better. The work lives at the seam: code Google can crawl, content a language model can cite, and numbers that hold up under review.
about.credentialsNote: Every degree and certification is available for review in a public folder. None of this asks you to take my word for it.

contact.subtitle: Tell me what's broken, or what you want to build.
contact.lead: The more specific your message, the more useful my first reply. If you already have the URL, Search Console access, or a Lighthouse report, send them: I'll come to the call with hypotheses instead of questions.
